name: Historic Centre of Agadez
description: Agadez sits on the southern edge of the Sahara in Niger and has long been known as the gateway to the desert. Its old centre grew in the 15th and 16th centuries, when Tuareg families settled here and left a maze of lanes that follows their former camp boundaries. Mud-brick houses and palaces fill eleven quarters, crowned by a 27-metre mud-brick minaret, the tallest of its kind in the world.
